instructions: Cut along the sausage casings with kitchen scissors and peel them off. Put the sausage meat in a large bowl with the 1 lb ground turkey, 1 tsp Worcestershire, 1 tsp Dijon, the 1/4 tsp salt and the 1/4 tsp pepper.
Mix it with your hands until it's evenly combined. It will feel wet and soft. Stop as soon as it's mixed. Overworked meat makes tough burgers.

Line a plate with parchment. With damp hands, shape the mixture into 4 patties about 1/2 inch thick and 4 1/2 inches across. Press a shallow dent into the middle of each one with your thumb, then put them in the fridge for 15 minutes so they hold together in the pan.
Meanwhile, wash and dry 4 lettuce leaves and slice the tomato.

Heat the 1 tbsp oil in a large cast iron or nonstick skillet over medium high until it shimmers. Lay in the patties, dent side up, and cook for 5 minutes without moving them, until the underside is deep brown and lets go of the pan.

Flip them and cook the other side for 4 to 5 minutes, until it's browned too. Turn the heat down a little if they're darkening too fast. You're cooking them to 165°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check one there. No thermometer? Cut into the middle of one: it's done when there's no pink left and the juices run clear.
Move the burgers to a plate to rest for 3 minutes. Meanwhile, toast the 4 buns cut side down in the same skillet over medium for about 1 minute, until golden.
Taste a corner of one patty. If it's flat, sprinkle a pinch more salt over the hot burgers.
Serve on the toasted buns with the mayonnaise, lettuce and tomato.
method_notes: All three bind ground turkey with Worcestershire and form patties about 1/2 inch thick, cooked to 165°F and served on toasted buns. Once Upon a Chef (the lead) mixes lean ground turkey with Italian turkey sausage for fat and flavor, adds only Dijon, Worcestershire and pepper, chills the wet patties and cooks them on a hot grill. Well Plated adds panko, an egg and tomato paste and cooks the patties in a hot cast iron skillet, and Chef Lola's Kitchen adds Parmesan, parsley and garlic and presses a dent into each patty so it stays flat. This one follows the lead's sausage mix but cooks it in a skillet, uses sweet sausage so the burgers stay mild, and takes the thumb dent from Chef Lola's Kitchen.
